chapterNote: Among the hardest psalms in the Psalter to translate and one of the grandest to hear: a processional, sung as the ark goes up, that begins with Moses' words at every breaking of camp — let God arise, let His enemies be scattered — and ends with the kingdoms of the earth singing. It moves like a parade. God rides through the wilderness and Sinai quakes; He shakes out a generous rain on a worn-out inheritance; He is a father of the orphan and a judge for widows in His holy dwelling, and He seats the solitary in a household and marches prisoners out into prosperity. The Lord gives the word and a great army of women carry the news; kings of armies flee and flee again, and the woman who stayed at home divides the plunder. Bashan's great massif looks with envy at the little hill God wanted for His home. Then the line the church has long held: You went up on high, You led captivity captive, You received gifts among men — which Paul, in Ephesians 4:8, turns around into gifts given to men, reading the ascent as Christ's. Blessed be the Lord, who day after day carries the load for us. The end widens past Israel: Egypt sends envoys, Cush stretches out her hands to God, and every kingdom is told to sing to the One who rides the ancient heavens and gives strength to His people.

1.text: For the choir director. A psalm of David. A song. Let God arise; let His enemies be scattered; let those who hate Him flee from before His face.
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach], A Psalm [mizmor] or Song [shir] of David. Let God [Elohim] arise [qum], let His enemies [oyeb] be scattered [puts]: let them also that hate [sane] Him flee [nus] before ['from his face', panim, the KJV margin] Him.
1.notes: yaqum Elohim yaphutsu oyebav (H6965, H430, H6327, H341): let God ARISE, let His enemies scatter — ve-yanusu mesanav mi-panav (H5127, H8130, H6440): let His haters flee from His FACE, the margin's literal. The words Moses said every time the ark set out (Numbers 10:35): the psalm is a processional, and its first line is a marching order a thousand years old.

2.text: As smoke is blown away, drive them away; as wax melts before the fire, let the wicked perish before the face of God.
2.amp: As smoke is driven away, so drive them away: as wax melts before [panim] the fire [esh], so let the wicked [rasha] perish [abad] at the presence [panim] of God [Elohim].
2.notes: ke-hinnadeph ashan tindoph (H5086, H6227): as smoke is DRIVEN, drive them — ke-himmes donag mi-pene-esh (H4549, H1749, H784): as wax melts from the face of fire; yobedu reshaim mi-pene Elohim (H6, H7563, H430): let the wicked perish from the face of God. Two things that cannot hold their shape near heat or wind: the psalm's estimate of organized opposition (cf. Micah 1:4).

3.text: But let the righteous be glad; let them exult before God; let them rejoice with gladness.
3.amp: But let the righteous [tsaddiq] be glad [samach]; let them rejoice [alats — exult] before [panim] God [Elohim]: yea, let them exceedingly ['rejoice with gladness', simchah, the KJV margin] rejoice [sus].
3.notes: ve-tsaddiqim yismechu yaaltsu liphne Elohim (H6662, H8055, H5970, H6440, H430): let the righteous be glad, let them EXULT before God's face — the same face that melts the wicked (v. 2) is the face the righteous celebrate in front of; ve-yasisu be-simchah (H7797, H8057): and let them rejoice 'with gladness', the margin's literal: three joy-verbs stacked in one verse.

4.text: Sing to God, make music to His name; build up a road for the One who rides through the deserts — Yah is His name — and exult before Him.
4.amp: Sing [shir] unto God [Elohim], sing praises [zamar] to His name [shem]: extol [salal — cast up a highway for] Him that rides upon the heavens [arabah — desert plains] by His name [shem] JAH [Yah], and rejoice [alaz] before [panim] Him.
4.notes: shiru l-Elohim zammeru shemo (H7891, H430, H2167, H8034): sing, make music to His name. sollu la-rokheb ba-arabot (H5549, H7392, H6160): CAST UP A HIGHWAY for the One riding through the arabot — salal, the road-building verb of Isaiah 62:10 — 'cast up, cast up the highway' (Isaiah 40:3 builds its highway in the arabah with the cognate noun); arabah is the desert plain, though many read it as the clouds, since Canaanite poetry calls Baal the cloud-rider and the psalm may be answering that. be-Yah shemo (H3050): 'in Yah is His name' — the short Name that stands at the end of every hallelujah.

5.text: A father of the fatherless and a judge for widows is God in His holy dwelling.
5.amp: A father [ab] of the fatherless [yatom], and a judge [dayyan] of the widows [almanah], is God [Elohim] in His holy [qodesh] habitation [maon — dwelling].
5.notes: abi yetomim ve-dayyan almanot (H1, H3490, H1781, H490): father of orphans and JUDGE of widows — dayyan, the court officer: not merely kind to them but their assigned advocate, the role Exodus 22:22-24 and Deuteronomy 10:18 give Him; Elohim bi-meon qodsho (H430, H4583, H6944): God in His holy dwelling. The rider of the deserts keeps a legal-aid office.

6.text: God settles the solitary in a household; He marches prisoners out into prosperity — but the rebellious live in a scorched land.
6.amp: God [Elohim] sets [yashab] the solitary [yachid] in families ['in a house', bayith, the KJV margin]: He brings out [yatsa] those which are bound [asir — prisoners] with chains: but the rebellious [sarar] dwell [shakan] in a dry land.
6.notes: Elohim moshib yechidim baytah (H430, H3427, H3173, H1004): God SEATS the solitary ones 'in a house', the margin's literal — yachid, the only-one, the word for Isaac in Genesis 22:2: the loneliest word in Hebrew, given an address. motsi asirim ba-kosharot (H3318, H615, H3574): He brings prisoners out into kosharot — prosperity, or, as the WEB and the old versions read it, with singing. akh sorerim shakhenu tsechichah (H5637, H7931, H6707): but the stubborn inhabit a parched place. God's household policy in one verse (cf. Acts 12:7-10).

7.text: O God, when it was You who went out at the head of Your people, when You strode across the wasteland, Selah:
7.amp: O God [Elohim], when You went forth [yatsa] before [panim] Your people [am], when You did march through the wilderness; Selah [Selah]:
7.notes: Elohim be-tsetkha liphne ammekha (H430, H3318, H6440, H5971): God, when You went OUT before Your people — the pillar of cloud leading the column (Exodus 13:21); be-tsadkha bi-shimon (H6805, H3452): when You STRODE through the desert — tsaad, a deliberate marching step. The sentence is left hanging on a Selah, and verse 8 finishes it with an earthquake. Deborah's song has the same lines (Judges 5:4-5).

8.text: the earth shook, the heavens also poured down at the presence of God — Sinai itself, at the presence of God, the God of Israel.
8.amp: The earth [eretz] shook [raash], the heavens [shamayim] also dropped [nataph] at the presence [panim] of God [Elohim]: even Sinai itself [zeh] was moved at the presence [panim] of God [Elohim], the God [Elohim] of Israel [Yisrael].
8.notes: erets raashah aph-shamayim nathephu (H776, H7493, H8064, H5197): the earth QUAKED, the heavens dripped — nataph, to drop, of rain. mi-pene Elohim zeh Sinai (H6440, H430, H2088, H5514): from the face of God — 'this Sinai', an old and difficult phrase the KJV reads as 'even Sinai itself' and others as the title 'the One of Sinai'. mi-pene Elohim Elohe Yisrael (H3478): from the face of God, the God of Israel. Sinai as weather, not geology.

9.text: You shook out a generous rain, O God; when Your inheritance was exhausted, You Yourself made it firm.
9.amp: You, O God [Elohim], did send ['shake out', nuph, the KJV margin] a plentiful [nedabah — freewill] rain, whereby You did confirm ['confirm it', kun, the KJV margin] Your inheritance [nachalah], when it was weary [laah].
9.notes: geshem nedabot taniph Elohim (H1653, H5071, H5130, H430): a rain of nedabot — freewill offerings, generosity — You SHOOK OUT, the margin's verb, the same nuph as the wave offering: rain waved over the land like a gift at the altar. nachalatekha ve-nilah attah khonantah (H5159, H3811, H3559): Your inheritance, and it was WEARY — You Yourself established it. The God of the earthquake is also the God of the growing season.

10.text: Your living company settled in it; in Your goodness, O God, You provided for the poor.
10.amp: Your congregation [chay — living company] has dwelt [yashab] therein: You, O God [Elohim], have prepared [kun] of Your goodness [tov] for the poor [ani — afflicted].
10.notes: chayyatekha yashebu-bah (H2416, H3427): Your chayyah — literally 'Your living thing', used of a company or a flock — settled in it; takhin be-tovatekha le-ani Elohim (H3559, H2896, H6041, H430): You PREPARE in Your goodness for the afflicted, God. The land was conquered by the God of verse 8 and then farmed by the God of verse 9, and the point of it was the poor.

11.text: The Lord gives the word; the women who carry the news are a great army:
11.amp: The Lord [Adonai] gave [natan] the word [omer]: great [rab] was the company ['army', tsaba, the KJV margin] of those that published [basar — brought good news] it.
11.notes: Adonai yitten-omer (H136, H5414, H562): the Lord GIVES the word — ha-mebasserot tsaba rab (H1319, H6635, H7227): the women bringing the news are a great HOST, the margin's 'army'. The participle is feminine plural: the victory-singers who met returning armies (Exodus 15:20-21; 1 Samuel 18:6), here drafted as an army of their own. basar is the verb behind 'gospel'.

12.text: 'Kings of armies flee, they flee!' — and the woman who stayed at home divides the plunder.
12.amp: Kings of armies [tsaba] did flee apace: and she that tarried [naveh — at home] at home [bayith] divided [chalaq] the spoil.
12.notes: malkhe tsebaot yiddodun yiddodun (H4428, H6635, H5074): kings of armies FLEE, FLEE — 'did flee, did flee', the margin's literal, the verb doubled for a rout; u-nevat bayit techalleq shalal (H5116, H1004, H2505, H7998): and the one who stayed at home divides the loot. The last person anyone would have counted on the roster gets the spoils, which is verse 6's policy applied to war.

13.text: Though you lie down among the sheepfolds, you will be like the wings of a dove sheathed in silver, her pinions in yellow gold.
13.amp: Though you have lain [shakab] among the pots, yet shall you be as the wings [kanaph] of a dove [yonah] covered [chaphah] with silver [keseph], and her feathers [ebrah] with yellow gold.
13.notes: im-tishkebun ben shephattayim (H7901, H8240): though you lie down between the shephattayim — the sheepfolds, or the campfire hearths, or the saddlebags; the word is rare and disputed (Judges 5:16 has it of Reuben staying by the sheepfolds). kanphe yonah nechpah ba-keseph (H3671, H3123, H2645, H3701): the wings of a dove sheathed in silver, ve-ebroteha bi-raqraq charuts (H84, H3422, H2742): her pinions in green-gold. The image is of plunder, or of the transformed people themselves: those who stayed behind come out shining.

14.text: When the Almighty scattered kings there, it was as if snow fell on Zalmon.
14.amp: When the Almighty [Shaddai] scattered [paras] kings in it ['for her, she', bah, the KJV margin], it was white as snow in Salmon.
14.notes: be-phares Shaddai melakhim bah (H6566, H7706, H4428): when SHADDAI — the Almighty, the patriarchs' name for God (Genesis 17:1) — spread kings out in her; tashleg be-Tsalmon (H7949, H6756): it snowed on Zalmon. Either the bleached bones and abandoned gear looked like snowfall, or the snow on the dark mountain ('Zalmon' means shady) is the picture of a rout turning the landscape white. The psalm is content to leave it strange.

15.text: A mountain of God is the mountain of Bashan; a many-peaked mountain is the mountain of Bashan.
15.amp: The hill [har] of God [Elohim] is as the hill [har] of Bashan; an high hill [har] as the hill [har] of Bashan.
15.notes: har-Elohim har-Bashan (H2022, H430, H1316): a mountain of God — the Hebrew idiom for a mighty one — is the mountain of Bashan; har gabnunnim har-Bashan (H1386): a mountain of many peaks is Bashan's. Bashan is the great basalt massif east of the Jordan, Hermon's country: the psalm sets up the biggest mountain it knows in order to have it envy a small ridge in verse 16.

16.text: Why do you look with envy, you many-peaked mountains, at the mountain God desired for His dwelling? Yes, the LORD will dwell there forever.
16.amp: Why leap you, you high hills [har]? this is the hill [har] which God [Elohim] desires [chamad] to dwell in [yashab]; yea, the LORD [YHWH] will dwell [shakan] in it for ever [netsach].
16.notes: lammah teratsdun harim gabnunnim (H7520, H2022, H1386): why do you WATCH ENVIOUSLY, you many-peaked mountains — a rare verb, perhaps to look askance, perhaps to leap. ha-har chamad Elohim le-shibto (H2530, H430, H3427): the mountain God DESIRED for His seat — chamad, the coveting-word of the tenth commandment, here of God choosing Zion. aph-YHWH yishkon la-netsach (H3068, H7931, H5331): indeed the LORD will dwell there forever. Election is not about size (Deuteronomy 7:7).

17.text: The chariots of God are twice ten thousand, thousands upon thousands; the Lord is among them — come from Sinai into the sanctuary.
17.amp: The chariots of God [Elohim] are twenty thousand, even ['even many thousands', eleph, the KJV margin] thousands [eleph] of angels: the Lord [Adonai] is among them, as in Sinai, in the holy [qodesh] place.
17.notes: rekheb Elohim ribbotayim alphe shinan (H7393, H430, H7239, H505, H8136): the chariotry of God is two myriads, thousands repeated — shinan is obscure, taken as 'repeated thousands' or 'angels'; Adonai bam Sinai ba-qodesh (H136, H5514, H6944): the Lord among them — Sinai in the sanctuary. The mountain has moved into the temple: the God who came down in fire now keeps His address in Jerusalem (cf. Deuteronomy 33:2; Hebrews 12:22).

18.text: You went up on high; You led captivity captive; You received gifts among men — even among the rebellious — that Yah God might dwell there.
18.amp: You have ascended [alah] on high [marom], You have led captivity captive: You have received [laqach] gifts for ['in the man', adam, the KJV margin] men [adam]; yea, for the rebellious [sarar] also, that the LORD [Yah] God [Elohim] might dwell [shakan] among them.
18.notes: alita la-marom shabita shebi (H5927, H4791, H7617, H7628): You went UP to the height, You took captivity captive — the conqueror's ascent with his prisoners behind him. laqachta mattanot ba-adam (H3947, H4979, H120): You received gifts 'in the man', the margin's literal — tribute from the conquered. ve-aph sorerim li-shkon Yah Elohim (H5637, H7931, H3050): even the rebellious, so that Yah God might dwell there. Paul quotes the verse in Ephesians 4:8 with 'gave gifts to men' — reading the ascent as Christ's, and the tribute a conqueror takes as the spoil He hands out to His church.

19.text: Blessed be the Lord, who day after day carries the load for us — the God of our salvation. Selah.
19.amp: Blessed [barak] be the Lord [Adonai], who daily [yom] loads [amas — bears our burden] us with benefits, even the God [El] of our salvation [yeshuah]. Selah [Selah].
19.notes: barukh Adonai yom yom yaamos-lanu (H1288, H136, H3117, H6006): blessed be the Lord — day by day He CARRIES for us: amas, to load up a pack animal; the Hebrew can mean He loads us with good or that He shoulders our load, and the WEB takes the second, which Isaiah 46:3-4 settles by having God carry Israel from the womb to old age. ha-El yeshuatenu (H410, H3444): the God of our salvation. Selah.

20.text: Our God is a God of acts of salvation; and to the LORD, the Lord, belong the ways out of death.
20.amp: He that is our God [El] is the God [El] of salvation [moshaah]; and unto GOD the Lord [Adonai] belong the issues from death [mavet].
20.notes: ha-El lanu El le-moshaot (H410, H4190): the God for us is a God of SALVATIONS, plural; ve-l-YHWH Adonai la-mavet totsaot (H3069, H136, H4194, H8444): and to the LORD, the Lord, belong the totsaot from death — the goings-out, the exits. Death has doors, and God holds the keys to them (cf. Revelation 1:18); the verse has long been read at Christian gravesides that know it.

21.text: But God will shatter the head of His enemies, the hairy scalp of the man who keeps walking on in his guilt.
21.amp: But God [Elohim] shall wound [machats — shatter] the head [rosh] of His enemies [oyeb], and the hairy scalp of such an one as goes on still [halak] in his trespasses [asham — guilt].
21.notes: akh-Elohim yimchats rosh oyebav (H430, H4272, H7218, H341): but God will SHATTER the head of His enemies — machats, a crushing blow; qodqod sear mithallekh ba-ashamav (H6936, H8181, H1980, H817): the hairy crown of the one WALKING ON in his guilt — the long-haired warrior, and the participle makes it a settled habit, not a stumble. The head-crushing of Genesis 3:15 in a battle hymn.

22.text: The Lord has said: 'Out of Bashan I will bring you back; out of the sea's depths I will bring you back,
22.amp: The Lord [Adonai] said [amar], I will bring again [shub] from Bashan, I will bring my people again [shub] from the depths of the sea [yam]:
22.notes: amar Adonai mi-Bashan ashib (H559, H136, H1316, H7725): the Lord said, from Bashan I will BRING BACK — ashib mi-metsulot yam (H4688, H3220): I will bring back from the sea's depths. The two extremes of the map, the high country and the deep water: wherever His people have been scattered or His enemies have hidden, He fetches them (cf. Amos 9:2-3).

23.text: so that your foot may wade in blood, and the tongues of your dogs may have their share of the enemies.'
23.amp: That your foot [regel] may be dipped ['red', machats, the KJV margin] in the blood [dam] of your enemies [oyeb], and the tongue [lashon] of your dogs in the same.
23.notes: lemaan timchats raglekha be-dam (H4272, H7272, H1818): so that you may WADE — the same machats as verse 21's shattering, here of a foot in blood, the margin's 'red' — oyebim minnehu (H341): from the enemies; leshon kelabekha (H3956, H3611): the tongue of your dogs, its portion from them. The grimmest image in the psalm, and the plainest statement that the victory is not metaphorical (cf. 1 Kings 21:19).

24.text: They have seen Your processions, O God — the processions of my God, my King, into the sanctuary.
24.amp: They have seen [raah] Your goings, O God [Elohim]; even the goings of my God [El], my King [melek], in the sanctuary [qodesh].
24.notes: rau halikhotekha Elohim (H7200, H1979, H430): they have SEEN Your processions, God — halikhah, a going, a march; halikhot Eli malki ba-qodesh (H410, H4428, H6944): the processions of my God, my King, into the holy place. The parade of verses 24-27 is the ark being carried up (2 Samuel 6:12-15), and the crowd can see it.

25.text: The singers went in front, the musicians after, in the middle the young women beating tambourines.
25.amp: The singers [shir] went before [qadam], the players on instruments [nagan] followed after [achar]; among [tavek] them were the damsels playing with timbrels.
25.notes: qiddemu sharim achar noganim (H6923, H7891, H310, H5059): the singers went FIRST, the string-players after; be-tokh alamot tophephot (H8432, H5959, H8608): in the middle, young women drumming — alamot, and topheph, to beat a tambourine, Miriam's instrument (Exodus 15:20). The order of march is preserved because someone was watching and wrote it down.

26.text: 'Bless God in the assemblies — the Lord, from the fountain of Israel!'
26.amp: Bless [barak] you God [Elohim] in the congregations, even the Lord ['ye that are of the fountain of Israel', maqor, the KJV margin], from the fountain [maqor] of Israel [Yisrael].
26.notes: be-maqhelot barekhu Elohim (H4721, H1288, H430): in the assemblies BLESS God; Adonai mi-meqor Yisrael (H136, H4726, H3478): the Lord, from the fountain of Israel — the margin reads it of the singers, 'you who are of the fountain of Israel', meaning the nation's stock or spring (cf. Deuteronomy 33:28; Isaiah 48:1). Either way the singing is family business.

27.text: There is little Benjamin leading them, the princes of Judah in their throng, the princes of Zebulun, the princes of Naphtali.
27.amp: There is little Benjamin with their ruler, the princes [sar] of Judah and their council, the princes [sar] of Zebulun, and the princes [sar] of Naphtali.
27.notes: sham Binyamin tsair rodem (H1144, H6810, H7287): there, little Benjamin RULING them — the smallest tribe (1 Samuel 9:21) at the head, Saul's tribe and Paul's. sare Yehudah rigmatam (H8269, H3063, H7277): the princes of Judah in their throng. sare Zebulun sare Naphtali (H2074, H5321): Zebulun's and Naphtali's princes — two from the far south, two from the far north: the whole country in one procession.

28.text: Your God has commanded your strength; make strong, O God, what You have worked for us.
28.amp: Your God [Elohim] has commanded [tsavah] your strength [oz]: strengthen [azaz], O God [Elohim], that which [zu] You have wrought [paal] for us.
28.notes: tsivvah Elohekha uzzekha (H6680, H430, H5797): your God has COMMANDED your strength — ordered it into being; uzzah Elohim zu paalta lanu (H5810, H2098, H6466): be strong, God, in what You have worked for us. The prayer of a people asking God to defend His own record.

29.text: Because of Your temple at Jerusalem, kings will bring You tribute.
29.amp: Because of Your temple [hekal] at Jerusalem shall kings bring [yabal] presents unto You.
29.notes: me-hekhalekha al-Yerushalaim (H1964, H3389): from Your temple above Jerusalem; lekha yobilu melakhim shai (H2986, H4428, H7862): to You kings will CONVEY tribute — yabal, the verb for leading a procession of gifts (Isaiah 18:7). The queen of Sheba's caravan, and the magi's, both travel on this line.

30.text: Rebuke the beast of the reeds, the herd of bulls with the calves of the peoples, until each one submits himself with pieces of silver; scatter the peoples who delight in war.
30.amp: Rebuke [gaar] the company ['the beasts of the reeds', chay qaneh, the KJV margin] of spearmen [qaneh — reeds], the multitude [edah] of the bulls [abbir], with the calves of the people [am], till every one submit himself with pieces of silver [keseph]: scatter ['he scattereth', bazar, the KJV margin] You the people [am] that delight [chaphets] in war [qerab].
30.notes: gaar chayyat qaneh (H1605, H2416, H7070): REBUKE the beast of the reed — the margin's 'beasts of the reeds': the hippopotamus or crocodile of the Nile, standing for Egypt (cf. Isaiah 27:1; Ezekiel 29:3); adat abbirim be-egle ammim (H5712, H47, H5695, H5971): the herd of bulls with the calves of the peoples — strong nations and their client states; bazzar ammim qerabot yechpatsu (H967, H7128, H2654): scatter the peoples who DELIGHT in war. The middle of the verse is obscure in Hebrew; every version reads the silver differently, and this one follows the KJV's submission with tribute rather than the trampling sense.

31.text: Envoys will come out of Egypt; Cush will hurry to stretch out her hands to God.
31.amp: Princes shall come out [athah] of Egypt; Ethiopia shall soon stretch out [ruts] her hands [yad] unto God [Elohim].
31.notes: yeethayu chashmannim minni Mitsrayim (H857, H2831, H4714): envoys will COME from Egypt — chashmannim, a word found only here, taken as nobles or bronze-bearers; Kush tarits yadav l-Elohim (H3568, H7323, H3027, H430): Cush will make her hands RUN to God — hurrying to surrender, or lifting them in prayer. The two great African powers of the psalmist's world, enrolled; Acts 8:27-39 puts a Cushite official on this road.

32.text: Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God; make music to the Lord, Selah,
32.amp: Sing [shir] unto God [Elohim], you kingdoms [mamlakah] of the earth [eretz]; O sing praises [zamar] unto the Lord [Adonai]; Selah [Selah]:
32.notes: mamlekhot ha-arets shiru l-Elohim (H4467, H776, H7891, H430): kingdoms of the earth, SING to God; zammeru Adonai (H2167, H136): make music to the Lord. The procession that began with one tribe's ark ends by handing the hymn book to every government on the map. Selah.

33.text: to the One who rides the ancient heaven of heavens — listen, He gives out His voice, a mighty voice.
33.amp: To Him that rides upon the heavens [shamayim] of heavens [shamayim], which were of old [qedem]; lo, He does send out ['give', natan, the KJV margin] His voice [qol], and that a mighty [oz] voice [qol].
33.notes: la-rokheb bi-shme shme-qedem (H7392, H8064, H6924): to the Rider on the heavens of ancient heavens — verse 4's rider, now above the sky rather than across the desert; hen yitten be-qolo qol oz (H5414, H6963, H5797): look, He GIVES with His voice a voice of strength, the margin's verb. The thunder of Psalm 29, heard from the end of a parade.

34.text: Ascribe strength to God! Over Israel is His majesty, and His strength is up in the skies.
34.amp: Ascribe [natan] you strength [oz] unto God [Elohim]: His excellency [gaavah — majesty] is over Israel [Yisrael], and His strength [oz] is in the clouds ['heavens', shachaq, the KJV margin].
34.notes: tenu oz l-Elohim (H5414, H5797, H430): ASCRIBE strength to God — kin to Psalm 29:1's habu, a different verb doing the same work of naming what is already His; al-Yisrael gaavato ve-uzzo ba-shechaqim (H3478, H1346, H7834): over Israel is His majesty and His strength is in the skies — the margin's 'heavens'. Both addresses at once: a nation and a universe.

35.text: Awesome are You, O God, from Your holy places; the God of Israel is the One who gives strength and might to His people. Blessed be God!
35.amp: O God [Elohim], You are terrible [yare] out of Your holy places [miqdash — sanctuary]: the God [El] of Israel [Yisrael] is He that gives [natan] strength [oz] and power to His people [am]. Blessed [barak] be God [Elohim].
35.notes: nora Elohim mi-miqdashekha (H3372, H430, H4720): AWESOME are You, God, from Your sanctuaries — nora, the fear-word made a title; El Yisrael hu noten oz ve-taatsumot la-am (H410, H3478, H5414, H5797, H8592, H5971): the God of Israel, He is the giver of strength and mightiness to the people; barukh Elohim (H1288): blessed be God. The psalm asked the congregation to give God strength (v. 34) and closes with God giving strength to them — which is the only direction it ever really travels.
